ask: Should back translation show as two rows, make it and check it, without changing the flows?
problem: Bezily's group thought a back translation needs a peer review. The screens put the two side by side, so it looks that way.
found: In the Standard flow, step 1 shows the peer check and back translation together, so it looks like one job. A finished back translation says "looks good", though no one checked it. The Spoken flow keeps them apart.
changed: Nothing yet. I only took pictures and drew a mockup. I will change no screen and no flow until you answer.
why: The words I propose: the row reads "Back translation · make it", then "Back translation · check it". A finished back translation says "made", not "looks good". The button after it says "Check the back translation". "Peer check" stays only where a flow has its own Peer Review step.
touches: Two options change the record screen and the text people read. One option also changes the Standard Bible Flow, which languages may already have copied. The Consultant Check would keep its own row.

options.label: Two rows, flows unchanged
options.result: Back translation shows as make it, then check it. The peer check keeps its own row. No flow changes.

options.label: Two rows, and a new step
options.result: As option one, and the Standard flow moves back translation into its own step after the peer check. Copied flows stay as they are.

options.label: New words only
options.result: Rows keep their order. Only the words change, and "looks good" becomes "made". The peer check still sits beside it.
